41.1.sa: प्रकृतीनां च तद्वाक्यं देशकालोपबृंहितम् । श्रुत्वा युधिष्ठिरो राजा सोत्तरं प्रत्यभाषत
41.1.en: Vaishampayana said Having listened to those words suitable to the hour and place, of his subjects, king Yudhishthira answered them saying,-"Great indeed must be the son of Pandu, whose merits, true or false, are thus recited by such foremost of Brahmanas assembled together. 'I shall now describe to you the means of conquering the senses as seen with the eye of the scriptures. A person, O king, will attain to the highest and by shaping his conduct accordingly.

41.2.sa: धन्याः पाण्डुसुता नूनं येषां ब्राह्मणपुङ्गवाः । तथ्यान्वाऽप्यथवाऽतथ्यान् गुणानाहुः समागताः

41.3.sa: अनुग्राह्या वयं नूनं भवतामिति मे मतिः । यदेवं गुणसम्पन्नानस्मान्ब्रूथ विमत्सराः
41.3.en: Forsooth, we are all your favourites, since you so freely describe us as possessing those accomplishment Amongst all living creatures man is said to be the foremost. Among men, the twice-born, persons well read in the Vedas are the foremost.

41.4.sa: धृतराष्ट्रो महाराजः पिता मे दैवतं परम् । शासनेऽस्य प्रिये चैव स्थेयं मत्प्रियकाङ्क्षिभिः
41.4.en: King Dhritarashtra, however, is our father and god. If you wish to do what is pleasing to me, always obey him and do what he likes. These last are considered as the souls of all living creatures. Indeed, those Brahmanas who have mastered the Vedas are considered as allseeing and omniscient. They are persons who have become conversant with Brahma.

41.5.sa: एतदर्थं हि जीवामि कृत्वा ज्ञातिवधं महत् । अस्य शुश्रूषणं कार्यं मया नित्यमतन्द्रिणा
41.5.en: Having killed all my kinsmen, I live for him alone. My great duty is to always serve him with particular care. As a blind man, without a guide, meets with many difficulties on a road, so has a person shorn of knowledge to meet with many impediments in the world. Therefore those who are endued with knowledge arc considered as superior to the rest.

41.6.sa: यदि चाहमनुग्राह्यो भवतां सुहृदां तथा । धृतराष्ट्रे यथापूर्वं वृत्तिं वर्तितुमर्हथ
41.6.en: If you, as also my friends, think that I should be a favourite with you and them, let me then request you all to treat Dhritarashtra as you used to do before. Those who wish to acquire virtue practise various rites according to the scriptural injunctions. They do not, however, attain to Liberation. They only acquire those good qualities which I shall presently mention.

41.7.sa: एष नाथो हि जगतो भवतां च मया सह । अस्यैव पृथिवी कृत्स्ना पाण्डवाः सर्व एव च
41.7.en: He is the master of the world, of yourselves, and of myself. The whole world with the Pandavas, is his. Purity of speech, of body, and of mind, forgiveness, truth, firmness and intelligence,-these good qualities are shown by pious persons who observe both kinds of religion.

41.8.sa: एतन्मनसि कर्तव्यं भविद्भर्वचनं मम । अनुज्ञाप्याथ तान् राजा यथेष्टं गम्यतामिति
41.8.en: You should always remember those words of mine.' The king then asked them to go where they liked. What is called Brahmacharya is considered as the means of attaining to Brahma. That is the foremost of all religions. It is by the practice of that religion that one acquires the highest end.

41.9.en: Having sent away the citizens and the people of the provinces, the Kuru king appointed his brother Bhimasena as Yuvaraja. Brahmacharya has no connection with the five vital airs, mind, understanding, the five senses of perception, and the five senses of action. It is, therefore, free from all the perceptions that the senses give. It is heard only as a word, and its form, is not seen, but can only be conceived.

41.10.sa: मन्त्रे च निश्चये चैव षाड्गुण्यस्य च चिन्तने । विदुरं बुद्धिसम्पन्नं प्रीतिमान्स समादिशत्
41.10.en: And he gladly appointed the highly intelligent Vidura for helping him with his advice and for looking after the sixfold requirements of the state. It is a state of existence only on the mind. It has no connection with the senses. That pure state should be attained to by the understanding alone.

41.11.sa: कृताकृतपरिज्ञाने तथाऽऽयव्ययचिन्तने । सञ्जयं योजयामास वृद्धं सर्वगुणैर्युतम्
41.11.en: And he appointed the old Sanjaya endued with every accomplishment, the superintendent of finances. He appointed Nakula superintendent of the forces, for giving them food and pay and for looking after other affairs of the army. He who practises it duly attains to Brahma; he who practises it half and half, attains to the status of the gods; while be who practises it indifferently, is born among Brahmanas and possessed of learning attains to eminence.

41.12.sa: बलस्य परिमाणे च भक्तवेतनयोस्तथा । नकुलं व्यादिशद्राजा कर्मणां चान्ववेक्षणे

41.13.sa: परचक्रोपरोधे च दुष्टानां चावमर्दने । युधिष्ठिरो महाराज फाल्गुनं व्यादिदेश ह
41.13.en: King Yudhishthira appointed Phalguna for resisting hostile forces and punishing the wicked. Brahmacharya is highly difficult to practise. Listen now to the means thereof. That twiceborn one who follows it should subdue the quality of Darkness as soon as it begins to show itself or as soon as it begins to be powerful.

41.14.sa: द्विजानां देवकार्येषु कार्येष्वन्येषु चैव ह । धौम्यं पुरोधसां श्रेष्ठं नित्यमेव समादिशत्
41.14.en: He appointed Dhaumya, the foremost of priests to attend daily to the Brahmanas and perform all rites in honour of the gods and all other religious rites. One who has taken that yow should not speak with women. He should never look at a naked woman. The sight of women, under even indifferent circumstances, excites the passion of all weak-minded men.

41.15.sa: सहदेवं समीपस्थं नित्यमेव समादिशत् । तेन गोप्यो हि नृपतिः सर्वावस्थो विशाम्पते
41.15.en: He appointed Sahadeva to always remain by his side, for the king thought, O king, that he should always be protected by that brother of his. as If a person feels a desire for women rising in his heart, he should observe the vow called Krichcchra and also pass three days in water. If desire is formed even in a dream, one should, diving in water, mentally repeat for three times the three Riks by Aghamarshana.

41.16.sa: यान्यानमन्यद्योग्यांश्च येषु येष्विह कर्मसु । तांस्तांस्तेष्वेव युयुजे प्रीयमाणो महीपतिः
41.16.en: The king cheerfully supported others in various other affairs according to their gratification. That wise man who follows this VOW should, with a liberal and enlightened mind, consume the sins in his mind which are created by the quality of Darkness.

41.17.sa: विदुरं सञ्जयं चैव युयुत्सुं च महामतिम् । अब्रवीत्परवीरघ्नो धर्मात्मा धर्मवत्सलः
41.17.en: That destroyer of hostile heroes, viz., the righteous-souled king Yudhishthira, devoted to virtue, commanded Vidura and the high-souled Yuyutsu, saying,-'You should always with attention and care do everything that my royal father Dhritarashtra desires. As the passage that carries away the refuge of the body is very closely connected with the body, so the embodied Soul is very closely connected with the body that confines it.

41.18.sa: उत्थायोत्थाय तत्कार्यमस्य राज्ञः पितुर्मम । सर्वं भवद्भिः कर्तव्यमप्रमत्तैर्यथायथम्

41.19.sa: पौरजानपदानां च यानि कार्याणि सर्वशः । राजानं समनुज्ञाप्य तानि कर्माणि भागशः
41.19.en: Everything for the citizens and the residents of the provinces should be done by you in your respective departments, after the king's permission. ever The different sorts of juices, passing through the network of arteries, nourish men's wind, bile, phlegm, blood, skin, flesh, intestines, bones, marrow, and the whole body.

42.1.sa: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा ज्ञातीनां ये हता युधि । श्राद्धानि कारयामास तेषां पृथगुदारधीः
42.1.en: Vaishampayana said After this the noble king Yudhishthira caused the Shraddha rites to be performed for every one of his kinsmen killed in battle. Bhishma said By being attached to objects of the senses which are always imbued with evil, living creatures become helpless. Those great persons, however, who are not attached to them, acquire the greatest end.

42.2.sa: धृतराष्ट्रो ददौ राजा पुत्राणामौर्ध्वदेहिकम् । सर्वकामगुणोपेतमन्नं गाश्च धनानि च
42.2.en: King Dhritarashtra also distributed, for the good of his dead sons, excellent food, and kine, and immense wealth, and many beautiful and costly gems amongst the Brahmanas. Seeing the world beset with the evils formed by birth, death, decrepitude, sorrow, disease, and anxieties, the man of intelligence should try for the attainment of Liberation.

42.3.sa: रत्नानि च विचित्राणि महार्हाणि महायशाः । युधिष्ठिरस्तु द्रोणस्य कर्णस्य च महात्मनः
42.3.en: Yudhishthira, accompanied by Draupadi, distributed much wealth for the sake of Drona and the great Karna, of Dhrishtadyumna and Abhimanyu, of the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha the son of Hidimba, and of Virata, and his other well-wishers who had served him loyally, and of Drupada and the five sons of Draupadi. He should be pure in words, thought and body; he should be shorn of pride. Of tranquil soul and endued with knowledge, he should live like a mendicant, and pursue happiness without being attached to any wordły object.

42.4.sa: धृष्टद्युम्नाभिमन्युभ्यां हैडिम्बस्य च रक्षसः । विराटप्रभृतीनां च सुहृदामुपकारिणाम्

42.5.sa: द्रुपदद्रौपदेयानां द्रौपद्या सहितो ददौ । ब्राह्मणानां सहस्राणि पृथगेकैकमुद्दिशन्

42.6.sa: धनै रत्नैश्च गोभिश्च वस्त्रैश्च समतर्पयत् । ये चान्ये पृथिवीपाला येषां नास्ति सुहृज्जनः
42.6.en: For each of these, the king pleased thousands of Brahmanas with presents of wealth, gems, kine and clothes. Again, if his mind is filled with attachment for mercy to creatures, he should, seeing that the universe is the result of acts, one should show indifference even to mercy itself.

42.7.sa: उद्दिश्योद्दिश्य तेषां च चक्रे राजौर्ध्वदेहिकम् । सभाः प्रपाश्च विविधास्तटाकानि च पाण्डव
42.7.en: The king performed the Shraddha rite for the good, in the next world, of every one of those kings also who had been killed in the battle without a single excepted kinsman or friend. Whatever good acts are done, or whatever sin is committed, the actor reaps the points thereof. Hence, one should, in words, thought, and deed, do only good acts.

42.8.sa: सुहृदां कारयामास सर्वेषामौर्ध्वदेहिकम् । स तेषामनृणो भूत्वा गत्वा लोकेष्ववाच्यताम्
42.8.en: And the king also, for the good of the souls of all his friends, set up houses for the distribution of food, and erected places for the distribution of water, and tanks to be excavated in their names. He enjoys happiness who practises abstention from injuring (others), truthfulness of speech, honesty towards all creatures, and forgiveness, and who is never careless.

42.9.sa: कृतकृत्योऽभवद्राजा प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन् । धृतराष्ट्रं यथापूर्वं गान्धारीं विदुरं तथा
42.9.en: Thus satisfying the debt he owed to them and warding off the chance of censure in the world, the king became happy and began to protect his subjects virtuously. Hence one, exercising his intelligence, should fix his mind, after training it, on peace towards all creatures.

42.10.sa: सर्वांश्च कौरवान्मान्यान्भृत्यांश्च समपूजयत् । याश्च तत्र स्त्रियः काश्चिद्धतवीरा हतात्मजाः
42.10.en: He showed due honour as before, to Dhritarashtra, and Gandhari, and Vidura, and to all the Kaurava elders and to all the officers. That man who considers the practice of the virtues mentioned above as the greatest duty as securing the happiness of all creatures, and as destroying all sorts of sorrow, is possessed of the greatest knowledge, and succeeds in acquiring happiness. Hence, one should, exercising his intelligence, fix his mind, after training it, on peace towards all creatures.

42.11.sa: सर्वास्ताः कौरवो राजा सम्पूज्यापालयद्घृणी । दीनान्धकृपणानां च गृहाच्छादनभोजनैः
42.11.en: The kind Kuru king honoured and protected all those ladies also who had, for the battle, been deprived of their heroic husbands and sons. One should never think of committing evil to others, One should not covet what is far above his power to acquire. One should not fix his thoughts on objects which are not real. One should, on the other hand, direct mind towards knowledge by continued exertions.

42.12.sa: आनृशंस्यपरो राजा चकारानुग्रहं प्रभुः । स विजित्य महीं कृत्स्नामानृण्यं प्राप्य वैरिषु । निःसपत्नः सुखी राजा विजहार युधिष्ठिरः
42.12.en: Freed from foes and having vanquished the whole Earth, king Yudhishthira began to enjoy great happiness." Ignorant persons bearing the weight of the world are like robbers laden with their booty of straggling sheep. The latter always avoid roads which are not favourable to them,

43.1.sa: अभिषिक्तो महाप्राज्ञो राज्यं प्राप्त युधिष्ठिरः । दाशार्हं पुण्डरीकाक्षमुवाच प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः
43.1.en: Having regained the kingdom, the highly pure and wise king Yudhishthira, after the ceremony of installation had been over, joining his hands together, addressed the louts-eyed Krishna of Dasharha's race, saying,-"Through your grace, O Krishna through your policy, might, intelligence and prowess, O foremost of the Yadus, I have regained this ancestral kingdom of mine. O you having lotus-eyes, I repeatedly bow to you, O chastiser of foes. Bhishma said The Yogin who wishes to always practise pure Brahmacharya and who is cognizant of the faults attaching to dreams, should, with his whole heart, try to give up sleep.

43.2.sa: तव कृष्ण प्रसादेन नयेन च बलेन च । बुद्ध्या च यदुशार्दूल तथा विक्रमणेन च

43.3.sa: पुनः प्राप्तमिदं राज्यं पितृपैतामहं मया । नमस्ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष पुनः पुनररिन्दम

43.4.sa: त्वामेकमाहुः पुरुषं त्वामाहुः सात्वतां पतिम् । नामभिस्त्वां बहुविधैः स्तुवन्ति प्रयता द्विजाः
43.4.en: You have been called the One only Being. You are the refuge of all worshippers. The Rishis worship you under various names. In dreams, the embodied soul, possessed by the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance, seems to become possessed of another body and move and act influenced by desire.

43.5.sa: विश्वकर्मन्नमस्तेऽस्तु विश्वात्मन्विश्वसम्भव । विष्णो जिष्णो हरे कृष्ण वैकुण्ठ पुरुषोत्तम
43.5.en: Salutation to you, O Creator of the Universe. You are the soul of the Universe. You are the soul of the Universe and the Universe has originated from you. You are Vishnu, you are Jishnu, you are Hari, you are Krishna, you are Vaikuntha, and you are the greatest of all beings. On account of application for acquiring knowledge and of continued reflection and recapitulation, the Yogin remains always awake. Indeed, the Yogin can keep himself continually awake by giving himself up to knowledge.

43.6.sa: अदित्याः सप्तधा त्वं तु पुराणो गर्भतां गतः । पृश्निगर्भस्त्वमेवैकस्त्रियुगं त्वां वदन्त्यपि
43.6.en: You have, as said in the Puranas, taken your birth seven times in the womb of Aditi. You also took birth in the womb of Prishni. The learned say that you are the three Yugas. Regarding this subject it has been asked what its this state in which the embodied creature thinks himself encircled by and engaged in objects and acts? It is true that the embodied being, with its senses really suspended, still considers itself to be possessed of body with all the sense of knowledge and of action.

43.7.sa: शुचिश्रवा हृषीकेशो घृतार्चिर्हंस उच्यते । त्रिचक्षुः शम्भुरेकस्त्वं विभुर्दामोदरोऽपि च
43.7.en: All your deeds are sacred. You are the master of our senses. You are the great Lord worshipped in sacrifices. You are called the great swan. You are three-eyed Shambhu. You are One, though known as Vibhu and Damodara. It is said that that master of Yoga, named Hari, perceives truly how it happens. The great Rishis say that the explanation given by Hari is correct and reasonable.

43.8.en: You are the great Boar you are Fire, you are the Sun, you have the emblem of bull on your banner, and you have Garuda also for your emblem. You are the grinder of inimical armies, you are the Being who perineates every form in the universe, and you are of irresistible power. The learned says that it is on account of the senses being exhausted with fatigue, dreams are seen by all creatures. The mind, however, never becomes inactive and hence arise dreams. This considered as their principal cause.

43.9.sa: वरिष्ठ उग्रसेनानीः सत्यो वाजसनिर्गुहः । अच्युतश्च्यावनोऽरीणां संस्कृतो विकृतिर्वृषः
43.9.en: You are the foremost of all things, you are dreadful, you are the commander of food, and you are Guha (the celestial commander-inchief). You yourself never suffer deterioration, you cause your enemies to fade and waste. You are the Brahmana of pure blood, and you are the issues of intermarriage. You are great. As the imagination of a person who is awake and engaged in acts, is due only to the creative power of the mind, similarly, the impressions in a dream belong only to the mind.

43.10.en: You move in the sky, you are called Vrishadarbha and Vrishakapi. You are Ocean, you are without attributes, you have three huinps, you have three abodes, and you create human forms of Earth, coming down from heaven. A person with desire and attachment receives those imaginations based upon the impressions of numberless pristine lives. Nothing, that impresses the mind once is ever lost, and the Soul being cognisant of all those impressions makes them appear.

43.11.sa: सम्राड् विराट् स्वराट् चैव सुरराजो भवोद्भवः । विभुर्भूरतिभूः कृष्णः कृष्णवर्त्मा त्वमेव च
43.11.en: You are Emperor, you are superior to Emperor, and even superior to him. You are King of the gods, and you are the root of Universe. You are all-powerful you are existence in every form, you are formless, you are Krishna, and you are fire. Whichever among the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance is caused by the influence of pristine acts and by whichever amongst them the mind is affected for the time being in whatever way, the elements in their subtile forms) or indicate accordingly (in the way of images).

43.12.sa: स्विष्टकृद्भिषजावर्तः कपिलस्त्वं च वामनः । यज्ञो ध्रुवः पतङ्गश्च यज्ञसेनस्त्वमुच्यसे
43.12.en: You are the Creator, you are the father of the celestial physicians, you are (the sage) Kapila, and you are the Dwarf. You are Sacrifice embodied, you are Dhruva, you are called Yajnasena. After images have thus been created the particular quality of Goodness Darkness or Ignorance that inay have been brought by pristine acts rises in the mind and produces its last result, viz., happiness or misery.

43.13.sa: शिखण्डी नहुषो बभ्रुर्दिवस्पृक् त्वं पुनर्वसुः । सुबभ्रू रुक्मयज्ञश्च सुषेणो दुन्दुभिस्तथा
43.13.en: You are Shikhandin, you are Nahusha, and you are Babhru. You are the constellation Punarvasu residing in the sky. You are of iwany colour, you are the sacrifice of Uktha, you are Sushena, you are the drum. Those images originating principally wind, bile, and phlegm, which men apprehend through ignorance and in consequence of tendency pervaded by Darkness and Ignorance, cannot, it has been said, be easily discarded.

43.14.sa: गभस्तिनेमिः श्रीपद्मः पुष्करः पुष्पधारणः । ऋभुर्विभुः सर्वसूक्ष्मश्चारित्रं चैव पठ्यसे
43.14.en: are The track of your car-wheels is light. You are the lotus of Prosperity, you are the cloud Pushkara, and you are adorned with garlands. You are rich, you are powerful you are the most subtile, and you are described in the Vedas. (When one is awake) whatever objects a person perceives in the mind through the senses in a clear state are apprehended by the mind in dreams while the senses are inactive.

43.15.sa: अम्भोनिधिस्त्वं ब्रह्मा त्वं पवित्रं धाम धामवित् । हिरण्यगर्भं त्वामाहुः स्वधा स्वाहा च केशव
43.15.en: You are the great sea, you are Brahman, you are the sacred refuge, and you know the residences of all. You called Hiranyagarbha, you are the sacred mantras swadha and svaha, you are Keshava. The Mind exists without obstruction in all things. This is due to the nature of the Soul. The Soul should be comprehended. All the elements and the objects they form exist in the Soul.

43.16.sa: योनिस्त्वमस्य प्रलयश्च कृष्ण त्वमेवेदं सृजसि विश्वमग्रे । विश्वं चेदं त्वद्वशे विश्वयोने नमोऽस्तु ते शार्ङ्गचक्रासिपाणे
43.16.en: You are the cause of all, and you are its dissolution. In the beginning you created the universe. This universe is under your sway, O Creator of the universe. Salutations to you, O wielder of Sharanga bow, discus, and sword. In the state called dreamless sleep the manifest human body which, of course, is the door of dreams, disappears in the mind. Possessing the body the mind enters the Soul which is unmanifest and upon which all existent and non-existent things depend, and becomes a wakeful witness with certainly of apprehension. Thus living in pure Consciousness which is the soul of all things, it is considered by the learned as transcending both Consciousness and all things in the universe.

43.17.sa: एवं स्तुतो धर्मराजेन कृष्णः सभामध्ये प्रीतिमान्पुष्कराक्षः । तमभ्यनन्दद्भारतं पुष्कलाभिर्वाग्भिर्ज्येष्ठं पाण्डवं यादवाग्र्यः
43.17.en: Thus hymned by king Yudhishthira in the midst of the assembly, the lotus-eyed Krishna became pleased. That foremost one of the Yadavas then began to cheer up the eldest son of Pandu with many sweet speeches. That Yogin who by desire covets any of the divine qualities (of Knowledge or renunciation, etc.,) should regard a pure mind to be at one with the object of his desire. All things exist in a pure mind or soul.

44.1.sa: ततो विसर्जयामास सर्वाः प्रकृतयो नृपः । विविशुश्चाभ्यनुज्ञाता यथास्वानि गृहाणि ते
44.1.en: Vaishampayana said, The king sent away all his subjects, who, ordered by the king, came back to their respective abodes. Bhishma said 'He does not know Brahma who does not know the four topics, namely, dreams, dreamless sleep, immanent, and transcendent Brahma, as also what is Manifest (viz., the body), and what is Unmanifest (the intelligence-soul), which the great Rishi (Narayana) has described as Tattvam (pure principle).

44.2.sa: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा भीमं भीमपराक्रमम् । सान्त्वयन्नब्रवीच्छ्रीमानर्जुनं यमजौ तथा
44.2.en: Solacing his brothers, Yudhishthira, shining with beauty, then addressed highly powerful brothers Bhima, Arjuna and the twins, saying,-Your bodies have, in the great battle, been wounded with various weapons by the foe. You are greatly tired, sorrow and anger have burnt your hearts. That which is manifest is subject to death. That which is unmanifest transcends, death. The Rishi Narayana has described the religion of inclination.

44.3.sa: शत्रुभिर्विविधैः शस्त्रैः क्षतदेहा महारणे । श्रान्ता भवन्तः सुभृशं तापिताः शोकमन्युभिः

44.4.sa: अरण्ये दुःखवसतीर्मत्कृते भरतर्षभाः । भवद्भिरनुभूता हि यथा कुपुरुषैस्तथा
44.4.en: Through my fault, O foremost of Bharata's race, you have suffered the miseries of banishment in the forests like ordinary men. Upon that depends the entire universe with its mobile and immobile creatures. The religion of disinclination again leads to the unmanifest and eternal Brahma.

44.5.sa: यथासुखं यथाजोषं जयोऽयमनुभूयताम् । विश्रान्ताल्लंब्यविज्ञानान् श्वः समेताऽस्मि वः पुनः
44.5.en: With great joy and ease enjoy this victory. After taking rest and refreshing your faculties, meet me again in the morning. The Creator (Brahman) has described the religion of inclination. Inclination indicates rebirth or return. Disinclination on the other hand, indicates the highest end.

44.6.en: After this, the mighty-armed Vrikodara, like Indra entering his own beautiful mansion, entered the palace of Duryodhana, that was decorated with many excellent buildings and rooms, that abounded with gems of various kinds, and that was full of servants male and female with the consent of Dhritarashtra. The ascetic who wish to discriminate exactly between good and evil, who is always bent on conceiving the nature of the Soul, and who devotes himself to the religion of disinclination, attains to that high end.

44.7.sa: धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञातं भ्रात्रा दत्तं वृकोदरः । प्रतिपेदे महाबाहुर्मन्दिरं मघवानिव

44.8.sa: यथा दुर्योधनगृहं तथा दुःशासनस्य तु । प्रासादमालासंयुक्तं हेमतोरणभूषितम्
44.8.en: The Mighty-armed Arjuna also, at the king's behest obtained the palace of Dushasana which was not inferior to Duryodhana's and which considered of many excellent mansions and was adorned with a golden gate-way, and which was full of riches and attendant of both sexes. One who wishes to accomplish this, should know both the Unmanifest and Purusha of which I shall speak now. That, again, which is different from both the Unmanifest and Purusha, and which transcends them both, and which is distinguished from all beings, should be particularly seen by an intelligent man. Both, Prakriti and Purusha are without beginning and without end. Both are incapable of being known by their likes.

44.10.en: The palace of Durmarshana was even superior to that Dushasana. Resembling the palace of Kubera himself, it was adorned with gold and every sort of gem. Both are eternal and indestructible. Both are greater than the greatest. They are similar in these. There are point of dissimilarity again between them.

44.11.sa: नकुलाय वरार्हाय कर्शिताय महावने । ददौ प्रीता महाराज धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः
44.11.en: King Yudhishthira gladly gave it to Nakula who deserved it best and who had been reduced with sufferings in the great forest. Prakriti is endued with the three qualities. It is also engaged in creation. The true attributes of Kshetrajna (Purusha or the Soul) are different.

44.12.sa: दुर्मुखस्य च वेश्माग्र्यं श्रीमत्कनकभूषणम् । पूर्णपद्मदलाक्षीणां स्त्रीणां शयनसङ्कुलम्
44.12.en: The best of palaces belonging to Durmukha was highly beautiful and adorned with gold. It was full of beds and beautiful women having eyes like lotus-petals. Purusha apprehends all the changes of Prakriti (but cannot be apprehended himself.) He transcends all qualities. As regards Purusha and the Supreme Soul again, both of them cannot be comprehended. Again for their both being without qualities by which they can be distinguished, both are greatly distinguished froin all else.

44.13.sa: प्रददौ सहदेवाय सन्ततं प्रियकारिणे । मुमुदे तच्च लब्ध्वाऽसौ कैलासं धनदो यथा
44.13.en: The king gave it to Sahadeva who was ever busy with doing what was agreeable to him. Obtaining it, Sahadeva became pleased as the king treasures upon obtaining Kailasa. The creation is the result of relation between Prakriti and Purusha (the soul), but we understand it by action. All movements come through the senses by person. "Who, I, This" etc. are only wordily statements.

44.14.sa: युयुत्सुर्विदुरश्चैव सञ्जयश्च विशाम्पते । सुधर्मा चैव धौम्यश्च यथास्वान् जग्मुरालयान्
44.14.en: Yuyutsu and Vidura and Sanjaya, O king, and Sudharman and Dhaumya, proceeded to their foriner abodes. A person putting on a turban has his head circled with three folds of a piece of cloth. Similarly the embodied Soul is invested with the three qualities of Goodness, and Ignorance. But though thus invested, the Soul is not identical with those qualities.

44.15.sa: सह सात्यकिना शौरिरर्जुनस्य निवेशनम् । विवेश पुरुषव्याघ्रो व्याघ्रो गिरिगुहामिव
44.15.en: Like a tiger entering his cave in the hills that foremost of men, viz., Krishna, accompanied by Satyaki, entered the palace of Arjuna. Hence these four topics, which are covered by these four considerations, should be understood. One who understands all this is never stupefied when he tries to form conclusions.

44.16.sa: तत्र भक्ष्यान्नपानैस्ते मुदिताः सुसुखोषिताः । सुखप्रबुद्धा राजानमुपतस्थुर्युधिष्ठिरम्
44.16.en: Feasting on the dishes and drinks, the princess passed the night in merriment. Awaking in the morning with delighted hearts, they approached the presence of the king Yudhishthira. He who wishes to secure high prosperity should become pure in mind, and practising austere practices regarding the body and the senses, should devote himself to yoga without seeking for fruits.

45.1.sa: प्राप्य राज्यं महाबाहुर्धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । यदन्यदकरोद्विप्र तन्मे वक्तुमिहार्हसि
45.1.en: Janamejaya said You should, O learned Brahmana, tell me what was next done by Yudhishthira the mighty-armed son of Dharma after he had regained his kingdom. By acting how, O you who are conversant with all courses of conduct, did Janaka the king of Mithila, versed in the religion of Liberation, succeed in acquiring Liberation, after casting off all worldly enjoyments?

45.2.sa: भगवान्वा हृषीकेशस्त्रैलोक्यस्य परो गुरुः । ऋषे यदकरोद्वीरस्तच्च व्याख्यातुमर्हसि
45.2.en: You should tell me also, O Rishi, what the heroic Hrishikesha, the supreme lord of the three worlds, did after this. “Regarding it is cited the following old narrative of the particular conduct by which that king, a master of all courses of conduct, succeeded in acquiring the highest happiness.

45.3.sa: शृणु तत्त्वेन राजेन्द्र कीर्त्यमानं मयाऽनघ । वासुदेवं पुरस्कृत्य यदकुर्वत पाण्डवाः
45.3.en: Hear me, O king, as I narrate fully, O sinless one, what the Pandavas, headed by Vasudeva did after this. There was a king in Mithila of the name of Janadeva of Janaka's race. He was ever engaged in thinking of the courses of conduct that might lead to the attainment of Brahma.

45.4.sa: प्राप्य राज्यं महाराज कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । चातुर्वर्ण्यं यथायोग्यं स्वे स्वे स्थाने न्यवेशयत्
45.4.en: Having regained his kingdom, O monarch, Kunti's son Yudhishthira made each of the four orders of men perform their respective duties. One hundred preceptors always used to live in his palace, describing to him the various courses of duty followed by people who had adopted the various modes of life.

45.5.sa: ब्राह्मणानां सहस्रं च स्नातकानां महात्मनाम् । सहस्रं निष्कमेकैकं दापयामास पाण्डवः
45.5.en: The (eldest) son of Pandu gave a thousand great Brahmanas of the Snataka order a thousand gold coins each. Well read in the Vedas, he was not very well satisfied with the speculations of his instructors on the nature of the Soul, and in their teachings of his extinction upon the dissolution of the body or of re-birth after death.

45.6.en: He then pleased the servants who were dependent on him and the guests who came to him, including persons who were undeserving, by satisfying their wishes. Once upon a time a great ascetic named Panchashikha the son of Kapila, having roamed over the whole world, arrived at Mithila.

45.7.sa: पुरोहिताय धौम्याय प्रादादयुतशः स गाः । धनं सुवर्णं रजतं वासांसि विविधान्यपि
45.7.en: He gave to his priest Dhaumya kine in thousands, and immense wealth and gold and silver and dresses of various kinds. Having made conclusions about the diverse duties connected with renunciation, he was above all pairs of opposites, and had no doubts.

45.8.sa: कृपाय च महाराज गुरुवृत्तिमवर्तत । विदुराय च राजाऽसौ पूजां चक्रे यतव्रतः
45.8.en: O monarch, the king treated Kripa like a preceptor. Ever observing vows the king continued to honour Vidura highly. He was considered as the foremost of Rishis. Living wherever he pleased, he wished to place before the reach of all men eternal happiness that is so difficult of attainment.

45.9.en: That foremost of charitable men satisfied all persons with presents of food and drink and dresses of various kinds and beds and seats. It appeared that he roamed, amazing the world, having put on the form of none else then that great Rishi, that lord of creatures, whom the followers of the Sankhya doctrine knew by the name of Kapila.

45.10.sa: लब्धप्रशमनं कृत्वा स राजा राजसत्तम । युयुत्सोर्धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पूजां चक्रे महायशाः
45.10.en: Having restored peace to his kingdom the highly illustrious king, O best of monarchs, paid due honours to Yuyutsu and Dhritarashtra. He was the greatest of all the disciples of Asuri and was called the undying. He had performed a mental Sacrifice lasting for a thousand years.

45.11.sa: धृतराष्ट्राय तद्राज्यं गान्धार्यै विदुराय च । निवेद्य सुस्थवद्राजा सुखमास्ते युधिष्ठिरः
45.11.en: Placing his kingdom at the disposal of Dhritarashtra, of Gandhari, and of Vidura, king Yudhishthira spent his days happily. He was firm in mind, and had performed all the rites and sacrifices that are enjoyed in the scriptures and that lead to the attainment of Brahma. He knew full well the five sacs that cover the Soul. He was devoted to the five acts regarding the adoration of Brahma, and had the five qualities. Know by the name of Panchashikha, he had approached one day a large assembly of Rishis following the Sankhya doctrines and enquired of them about the highest object of human acquisition, namely, the Unmanifest or that upon which the five sacs rest.

45.12.sa: तथा सर्वं स नगरं प्रसाद्य भरतर्षभ । वासुदेवं महात्मानमभ्यगच्छत्कृताञ्जलिः
45.12.en: Having pleased everybody, including the citizens, in this way, Yudhishthira, O foremost of Bharata's race, approached with joined hands the presence of the great Vasudeva. For acquiring a knowledge of the Soul, Asuri had enquired of his preceptor. On account of the latter's instructions and of his own penances, Asuri understood the distinction between the body and the Soul and had gained celestial vision.

45.13.sa: ततो महति पर्यङ्के मणिकाञ्चनभूषिते । ददर्श कृष्णमासीनं नीलमेघसमद्युतिम्
45.13.en: He saw Krishna, of the hue of a blue cloud, seated on a large sofa bedecked with gold and gems. In that assembly of ascetics, Asuri described the Immutable, One, and Indestructible Brahma which is seen in various forms.

45.14.sa: जाज्वल्यमानं वपुषा दिव्याभरणभूषितम् । पीतकौशेयवसनं हेम्नेवोपगतं मणिम्
45.14.en: Clad in yellow silk robes and adorned with celestial ornaments, his person shone effulgent like a jewel set on gold. Panchashikha became a disciple of Asuri. He lived on human milk. There was a certain Brahman lady named Kapila. She was Asuri's wife.

45.15.en: His bosom adorned with the Kaustubha gem, he shone like the mountain with the rising Sun. Panchashikha was accepted by her as a son and he used to suck her breasts. For this, he came to be known as the son of Kapila and his understanding became fixed on Brahma.

45.16.sa: नौपम्यं विद्यते तस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन । सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं विष्णुं पुरुषविग्रहम्
45.16.en: There was no equal of his beauty in three worlds, Approaching the great one who was an incarnation of Vishnu, king Yudhishthira addressed him sweetly and smilingly saying,-'O foremost of intelligent men, have you passed the night happily? The divine Rishi said to me, all this, regarding the circumstances of his birth and those about his becoming the son of Kapila. The latter also told me about the omniscience of Panchashikha.

45.17.sa: उवाच मधुरं राजा स्मितपूर्वमिदं तदा । सुखेन ते निशा कच्चिद्व्युष्टा बुद्धिमतां वर

45.18.sa: कच्चिज्ज्ञानानि सर्वाणि प्रसन्नानि तवाच्युत । तथैवोपश्रिता देवी बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतां वर
45.18.en: O you of unfading glory, have all your faculties been fully invigorated? O foremost of intelligent persons, is it all right with your understanding? Knowing fully all the forms of duty, Panchashikha, after having himself gained high knowledge, (came to Janaka) and knowing that that king had equal reverence for all his preceptors, began to startle those hundred preceptors (by a very sensible exposition of his doctrine).

45.19.sa: वयं राज्यमनुप्राप्ताः पृथिवी च वशे स्थिता । तव प्रसादाद्भगवंस्त्रिलोकगतिविक्रम
45.19.en: We have regained our kingdom and the whole Earth has come under our sway, O divine lord, through your favour, O refuge of the three worlds and, O you of three steps. Through your favour we have gained victory and obtained great fame and have not transgressed the duties of our order.' Marking the genius of the son of Kapila, Janaka became exceedingly attacked to him, and abandoning his hundred preceptors, began to follow him.

45.20.sa: जयं प्राप्ता यशश्चाग्र्यं न च धर्मच्युता वयम् । तं तथा भाषमाणं तु धर्मराजमरिन्दमम् । नोवाच भगवान्किञ्चिद्ध्यानमेवान्वपद्यत
45.20.en: The divine Krishna did not speak a single word to that chastiser of enemies, king Yudhishthira, for he was then rapt in meditation. Then Kapila's son began to discourse to Janaka, who had according to the ordinance bent his head to him and who was fully competent to understand the sage's instructions, upon that great religion of Liberation which is explained in Sankhya treatises.

46.1.sa: किमिदं परमाश्चर्यं ध्यायस्यमितविक्रम । कच्चिल्लोकत्रयस्यास्य स्वस्ति लोकपरायण
46.1.en: Yudhishthira said 'Wonderful it is, o you of immeasurable prowess, that you are rapt in meditation. O great refuge of the universe, is it all well with the three worlds? Bhishma said "Thus instructed by the great Rishi Panchashikha, Janadeva of the family of Janaka, once more asked him about the subject of existence or non-existence after death.

46.2.sa: चतुर्थं ध्यानमार्गं त्वमालम्ब्य पुरुषर्षभ । अपक्रान्तो यतो देवस्तेन मे विस्मितं मनः
46.2.en: When you have, O god, withdrawn yourself from the world, having, O foremost of men, adopted the fourth state (of perfect unconsciousness of the world) my mind has been filled with wonder. O illustrious one, if no person, retains any knowledge after departing from this state of existence, if, indeed, this is true, what then is the difference between Ignorance and Knowledge? What do we gain then by knowledge and what do we lose by ignorance?

46.3.sa: निगृहीतो हि वायुस्ते पञ्चकर्मा शरीरगः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रसन्नानि मनसि स्थापितानि ते
46.3.en: The five vital airs which act within the body have been controlled by you. You have controlled your senses within your mind. See, O foremost of the twice-born, that if liberation be such, then all religious acts and vows terminate only in annihilation? Of what use would then the distinction be between heedfulness and heedlessness.

46.4.sa: वाक्च सत्त्वं च गोविन्द बुद्धौ संवेशितानि ते । सर्वे चैव गुणा देवाः क्षेत्रज्ञे ते निवेशिताः
46.4.en: Both words and mind, O Govinda, have been concentered within your understanding. All your senses, have been withdrawn into your self. If Liberation means dissociation from all objects of pleasure or an association with objects that are not lasting, why should then men cherish a desire for action or having set themselves to action, continue to find out the necessary means for the accomplishment of desired ends? What then is the truth.

46.5.sa: नेङ्गन्ति तव रोमाणि स्थिरा बुद्धिस्तथा मनः । काष्ठकुड्यशिलाभूतो निरीहश्चासि माधव
46.5.en: The hair on your body stands erect. Your mind and understanding are both calm. You are as immobile now, O Madhava, as an wooden post or a stone? Bhishma said Seeing the king enveloped in thick darkness, stupefied by error, and become helpless, the learned Panchashikha put his mind at rest by once more addressing him thus.

46.6.sa: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो निरिङ्गो ज्वलते पुनः । तथाऽसि भगवन्देव पाषाण इव निश्चलः
46.6.en: O illustrious god, you are as calm as the flame of a lamp burning in a place where there is no wind. You are as immobile as a rock. In Liberation the consummation is not Extinction. Nur is that consummation any kind of Existence. What we see is a union of body senses, and mind. Existing independently as also depending on one another, these go on acting.

46.7.sa: यदि श्रोतुमिहार्हामि न रहस्यं च ते यदि । छिन्धि मे संशयं देव प्रपन्नायाभियाचते
46.7.en: If I am fit to hear the cause, and if it is no secret, remove, O god, my doubt, for I beg this। favour from you. The ingredients that form the body are water, ether, wind, heat, and earth. These exisi together according to their own nature. They become separated again according to their own nature.

46.8.sa: त्वं हि कर्ता विकर्ता च क्षरं चैवाक्षरं च हि । अनादिनिधनश्चाद्यस्त्वमेव पुरुषोत्तम
46.8.en: You are the Creator and you are the Destroyer. You are destructible and you indestructible. You are without beginning and you are without end. You are the first and the foremost of beings. Ether, wind, heat, water and earth,-these five objects in a state of union form the body. The body is not one element.

46.9.sa: त्वत्प्रपन्नाय भक्ताय शिरसा प्रणताय च । ध्यानस्यास्य यथा तत्त्वं ब्रूहि धर्मभृतां वर
46.9.en: O foremost of pious men, tell me the cause of this abstraction. I solicit your favour, and am your devoted worshipper, and am bending my head to you. Intelligence, stomachic heat, and the vital airs, called Prana, etc., that are all wind, three are the organs of action. The senses, the objects of the senses, the power by which they become capable of being perceived the faculties by which they succeed in perceiving them, the mind, the vital airs called Prana. Apana and the rest, and the various juices and humours that are the results of the digestive organs, flow from the three organs already named.

46.10.sa: ततः स्वे गोचरे न्यस्य मनोबुद्धीन्द्रियाणि सः । स्मितपूर्वमुवाचेदं भगवान्वासवानुजः
46.10.en: Thus accosted the illustrious younger brother of Vasava, reinstating his mind, understanding and the senses in their proper places, said these words similingly. Hearing, touch, taste, vision, and scent,-these are the five senses. They have derived their attributes from the mind which is their cause.

46.11.sa: शरतल्पगतो भीष्मः शाम्यन्निव हुताशनः । मां ध्याति पुरुषव्याघ्रस्ततो मे तद्गतं मनः
46.11.en: Vasudeva said 'That foremost men, viz., Bhishma, who is now lying on a bed of arrows, and who is now like a fire that is about to be extinguished, is thinking of me. It is therefore my mind also was concentrated on him. The mind, which is as an attribute of Chit, has three states, viz., pleasure, pain and absence of both pleasure and pain.

46.12.sa: यस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः । न सेहे देवराजोऽपि तमस्मि मनसा गतः
46.12.en: My mind was fixed in him the twang of whose bow and the sound of whose palms Indra himself was unable to bear. Sound, touch, form, taste, scent, and the objects to which they are attached these till the time of one's death are causes for the production of one's knowledge.

46.13.sa: येनाभिजित्य तरसा समस्तं राजमण्डलम् । ऊढास्तिस्त्रस्तुताः कन्यास्तमस्मि मनसा गतः
46.13.en: I was thinking of him who having defeated in a moment all the assembled kings, carried the three princesses of Kashi for the marriage of his brother Vichitravirya. Upon the senses depend all acts (leading to lucavon), as also renunciation (leading to the attainment of Brahma), and also the ! ascertainment of truth regarding all topics of enquiry. The learned say thai ascertainment of truth) is the highest end of existences, and is the root of Liberation and regarding Intelligence, they say that it leads to Liberation and Brahma.

46.14.sa: त्रयोविंशतिरात्रं यो योधयामास भार्गवम् । न च रामेण निस्तीर्णस्तमस्मि मनसा गतः
46.14.en: I was thinking of him who fought continually for twenty-three days with Rama himself of Bhrigu's race and whom Rama could not defeat. That person who considers this union of perishable attributes as the Soui, feeis, on account of such imperfect knowledge, unending misery

46.15.sa: एकीकृत्येन्द्रियग्रामं मनः संयम्य मेधया । शरणं मामुपागच्छत्ततो मे तद्गतं मनः
46.15.en: Controlling all his senses and concentrating his mind by the aid of his understanding, he sought my refuge. It was for this that I had fixed my mind upon him. Those persons, who, however, regard alll worldly objects as not-Soui, and who on that account cease to have any affection or attachment for them, have never to suffer any misery, for sorrow, in their case, stands in need of some foundation upon which to depend.

46.16.sa: यं गङ्गा गर्भविधिना धारयामास पार्थिव । वसिष्ठशिक्षितं तात तमस्मि मनसा गतः
46.16.en: I was thinking of him whom Ganga conceived and gave birth to, according to ordinary human laws and whom Vasishtha took as a pupil. About it there is the unrivalled branch of knowledge which treats of Renunciation. It is called Samyagvadha. I shall describe it to you. Listen to it for the sake of your Liberation.

46.17.sa: दिव्यास्त्राणि महातेजा यो धारयति बुद्धिमान् । साङ्गांश्च चतुरो वेदांस्तमस्मि मनसा गतः
46.17.en: I was thinking of that powerful hero of great intelligence who is a master of all the celestial weapons as also of the four Vedas with all their auxiliaries. Renunciation of acts is (laid down) for all persons who seek Liberation earnestly. They, however, who have not been instructed correctly have to bear a heavy load of sorrow,

46.18.sa: रामस्य दयितं शिष्यं जामदग्न्यस्य पाण्डव । आधारं सर्वविद्यानां तमस्मि मनसा गतः
46.18.en: I was thinking of him, O son of Pandu, who is the favourite disciple of Rama the son of Jamadagni, and who is the master of all the sciences. Vedic sacrifices and other rites exist for renunciation of wealth and other earthly (objects. For renunciation of all enjoyments, exist yows and fasts of various sorts. For renunciation of pleasure and happiness exist penances and yoga. Renunciation everything, is the highest kind of renunciation,

46.19.sa: स हि भूतं भविष्यच्च भवच्च भरतर्षभ । वेत्ति धर्मविदां श्रेष्ठं तमस्मि मनसा गतः
46.19.en: I was thinking of that best of all persons conversant with morality and duty, of him, O foremost of Bharatas, who knows the Past, the Future, and the Present. This that I shall presently describe to you is the one path pointed out by the learned for that renunciation of everything. They who follow that path succeed in driving off all sorrow. They, however, that deviate from it suffer distress and misery

46.20.sa: तस्मिन्हि पुरुषव्याघ्ने कर्मभिः स्वैर्दिवं गते । भविष्यति मही पार्थ नष्टचन्द्रेव शर्वरी
46.20.en: After the ascension to heaven of that foremost of kings for his own achievements the Earth, O son of Pritha, will took like a moonless night. First speaking of the five organs of knowledge having the mind for the sixth, und all of which live in the understanding, i stall describe the five organs of action having strength for their sixth.

46.21.sa: तद्युधिष्ठिर गाङ्गेयं भीष्मं भीमपराक्रमम् । अभिगम्योपसङ्गृह्य पृच्छ यत्ते मनोगतम्
46.21.en: Therefore, O Yudhishthira, humbly approaching Ganga's son, viz., Bhishma, ask him about what you may wish to learn. The two hands forms the two organs of action. The two legs are two organs for moving from one place to another. The sexual organ is for both pleasure and the continuation of in species. The lower channel, leading from the stomach downwards, is the organ for purging off of all used-up matter. aran a prafastarffuta usati fag: 1

46.22.sa: चातुर्विद्यं चातुर्होत्रं चातुराश्रम्यमेव च । राजधर्मांश्च निखिलान् पृच्छैनं पृथिवीपते
46.22.en: O king enquire of him about the four branches of knowledge, about sacrifices and the rites sanctioned for the four castes, about the four modes of life, and about the duties of kings. The organ of speaking exists for the expression of sounds. These five organs of action belong to the mind. These are the eleven organs of knowledge and of action. One should speedily cast off the inind with the understanding.

46.23.sa: तस्मिन्नस्तमिते भीष्मे कौरवाणां धुरन्धरे । ज्ञानान्यस्तं गमिष्यन्ति तस्मात्त्वां चोदयाम्यहम्
46.23.en: When Bhishma, that foremost one of Kuru's race, will disappear from the world every kind of knowledge will go away with him. It is, therefore, that I urge you to do it. In the act of hearing, three causes must exist simultaneously, viz., the two ears, sound, and the mind. The same is the case with the perception of touch; the same with that of form; the same with that of taste and smell.

46.24.sa: तच्छ्रुत्वा वासुदेवस्य तथ्यं वचनमुत्तमम् । साश्रुकण्ठः स धर्मज्ञो जनार्दनमुवाच ह
46.24.en: Hearing these wholesome and pregnant words of Vasudeva, the righteous Yudhishthira, with voice suppressed with tears, answered Janardana saying—'What you have said, O Madhava, about the greatness of Bhishma, is perfectly true. I have not the least doubt about it. These fifteen attributes are necessary for the several kinds of perception. In consequence of them, every man becomes conscious of three separate things regarding those perceptions.

46.25.sa: यद्भवानाह भीष्मस्य प्रभावं प्रति माधव । तथा तन्नात्र सन्देहो विद्यते मम माधव

46.26.sa: महाभाग्यं च भीष्मस्य प्रभावश्च महाद्युते । श्रुतं मया कथयतां ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्
46.26.en: I had heard of the piety and greatness, of the illustrious Bhishma from great Brahmanas talking about it. There are again three classes (of mental perception, viz., those that appertain to Goodness, those that belong of Darkness, and those that belong to Ignorance. With them are connected three kinds of consciousness, including all feelings and emotions.

46.27.sa: भवांश्च कर्ता लोकानां यद्ब्रवीत्यरिसूदन । तथा तदनभिध्येयं वाक्यं यादवनन्दन
46.27.en: You, O killer of foes, are the Creator of all the worlds, There, cannot, therefore, O delighter of the Yadavas, be the least doubt in what you say. Pleasure, satisfaction, joy, happiness, and tranquillity, originating in the mind from any perceptible cause or in the absence of any apparent cause, appertain to the quality of Goodness.

46.28.sa: यदि त्वनुग्रहवती बुद्धिस्ते मयि माधव । त्वामग्रतः पुरस्कृत्य भीष्मं यास्यामहे वयम्
46.28.en: If you are pleased to show us favour, O Madhava, then we shall go to Bhishma with yourself at our head. Discontent, regret, grief, cupidity, and vindictiveness, having no cause or occasioned by any perceptible cause, are the marks of the quality of Darkness.

46.29.sa: आवृत्ते भगवत्यर्के स हि लोकान् गमिष्यति । त्वद्दर्शनं महाबाहो तस्मादर्हति कौरवः
46.29.en: When the divine Sun shall have turned towards the north, Bhishma will leave (this world) for those blissful regions which he has acquired. That descendant of Kuru's race, therefore, O mighty-armed one, deserves to see you. Wrong judgement, stupefaction, carelessness, dreams, and sleepiness, however, caused, appertain to the quality of Ignorance.

46.30.sa: तव चाद्यस्य देवस्य क्षरस्यैवाक्षरस्य च । दर्शनं त्वस्य लाभः स्यात्त्वं हि ब्रह्ममयो निधिः
46.30.en: Bhishina will then see you who are the first of gods, and who destructible and indestructible. Indeed, O lord, you are the vast receptacle of Brahma. Whatever state of consciousness exists, regarding either the body or the mind, united with joy or satisfaction, should be considered as due to the quality of Goodness.

46.31.sa: श्रुत्वैवं धर्मराजस्य वचनं मधुसूदनः । पार्श्वस्थं सात्यकिं प्राह रथो मे युज्यतामिति
46.31.en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of king Yudhishthira, the destroyer of Madhu addressed Satyaki who was sitting by him, saying,–'Let my car be yoked. Whatever state of consciousness exists united with any feeling of discontent or depression should be considered as the outcome of the quality of Darkness.

46.32.sa: सात्यकिस्त्वाशु निष्क्रम्य केशवस्य समीपतः । दारुकं प्राह कृष्णस्य युज्यतां रथ इत्युत
46.32.en: are At this Satyaki quickly left Keshava's company and going out, ordered Daruka, saying,-'Let Krishna's car be made ready.' Whatever state, of the body or the body or the mind, exists with error or carelessness, is the outcome of Ignorance which is incomprehensible and inexplicable.

46.33.sa: स सात्यकेराशु वचो निशम्य रथोत्तमं काञ्चनभूषिताङ्गम् । मसारगल्वर्कमयैर्विभङ्गैर्विभूषितं हेमनिबद्धचक्रम्
46.33.en: Hearing the words of Satyaki, Daruka immediately yoked Krishna's car. That best of cars, adorned with gold, decked with profuse emeralds, and moon-gems and sun-gems furnished with golden wheels, effulgent, fleet as the wind, set in the middle with various other kinds of jewels, beautiful as the morning sun, equipped with a beautiful standard bearing the emblem of Gar::da, and numberless other banners, was yoked with those best of horses quick coursing as thought, viz., Sugriva and Saivya and the other two, in trappings of gold. Having yoked it, О tiger among kings, Daruka with joined palms, informed Krishna of the fact The organ of hearing rests on either; it is either itself (under limitations); Sound has that organ for its refuge. In perceiving sound, one may not immediately acquire a knowledge of the organ of hearing and of ether. But when sound is perceived, the organ of hearing and ether do not long remain unknown.

46.34.sa: दिवाकरांशुप्रभमाशुगामिनं विचित्रनानामणिभूषितान्तरम् । नवोदितं सूर्यमिव प्रतापिनं विचित्रतार्क्ष्यध्वजिनं पताकिनम्

47.1.sa: शरतल्पे शयानस्तु भरतानां पितामहः । कथमुत्सृष्टवान्देहं कं च योगमधारयत्
47.1.en: How did the grandfather of Bharatas, who lay on a bed of arrows, cast off his body and what sort of Yoga did he adopt? By doing what does one gain happiness, and what is that by doing which one meets with misery? What also is that, O Bharata, by doing which one becomes freed from fear and sojourns here successfully,

47.2.sa: शृणुष्वावहितो राजञ्शुचिर्भूत्वा समाहितः । भीष्मस्य कुरुशार्दूल देहोत्सर्गं महात्मनः
47.2.en: Listen, O king, with pure heart and rapt attention, as to how, O foremost of the Kurus, the great Bhishma renounced his body. Bhishma said The ancients who had there minds, directed to the Shrutis, spoke highly of the duty of selfcontrol for all the castes in general, but for the Brahmanas in especial.

47.3.sa: निवृत्तमात्रे त्वयन उत्तरे वै दिवाकरे । समावेशयदात्मानमात्मन्येव समाहितः
47.3.en: As soon as the Sun, passing the solstitial point entered in his northerly course, Bhishma with rapt attention, caused his soul (as connected with and independent of the body) to enter into the Universal Soul. One who is not self-controlled never enjoys success in religious rites. Religious rites, penances, truth, all these depend upon selfcontrol.

47.4.sa: विकीर्णांशुरिवादित्यो भीष्मः शरशतैश्चितः । शुशुभे परया लक्ष्या वृतो ब्राह्मणसत्तमैः
47.4.en: Surrounded by many foremost of Brahmanas, that hero, his body cut with innumerable arrows, shone like the sun with his innumerable rays. Self-control increases one's energy. Self-। control is said to be sacred. The man of selfcontrol becomes sinless and fearless and acquires great results.

47.5.sa: व्यासेन वेदविदुषा नारदेन सुरर्षिणा । देवस्थानेन वात्स्येन तथाऽश्मकसुमन्तुना
47.5.en: Surrounded by Vyasa conversant with the Vedas, by the celestial Rishi Narada, by Devasthana, by Ashmakasumantu, by Jaimini, by the great Paila, by Shandilya, by Devarata, by the highly intelligent Maitreya, by Asita and Vasishtha and the great Kaushika, by Harita and Lomasa and the highly intelligent Atri's son, by Brihaspati and Shukra and the great sage Chyavana, by Sanatkumara and Kapila and Valmiki and Tumvuru and Kuru, By Maudgalya and Rama of Bhrigu's race, and the great sage Trinavindu, by Pippalada and Vayu and Samvarta and Pulaha and Kacha, by Kashyapa and Pulastya and Kratu and Daksha and Parashara, by Marichi and Angiras and Kashyapa and Gautama and the sage Galava, by Dhaumya and Vibhanda and Mandavya and Dhaumra and Krishnanubhautika, by Uluka, that foremost of Brahmanas and the great sage Markandeya, by Bhaskari and Purana and Krishna and Suta, —that foremost of pious men, surrounded by these and many other saintly sages of great souls and endued with faith and self-control and equanimity of mind, the Kuru hero looked like the Moon surrounded by the planets and the stars. One who is self-controlled sleeps happily and wakes happily. He lives happily in the world and his mind always remains cheerful

47.6.sa: तथा जैमिनिना चैव पैलेन च महात्मना । शाण्डिल्यदेवलाभ्यां च मैत्रेयेण च धीमता

47.7.sa: असितेन वसिष्ठेन कौशिकेन महात्मना । हारीतलोमशाभ्यां च तथाऽऽत्रेयेण धीमता

47.8.sa: बृहस्पतिश्च शुक्रश्च च्यवनश्च महामुनिः । सनत्कुमारः कपिलो वाल्मीकिस्तुम्बुरुः कुरुः

47.9.sa: मौद्गल्यो भार्गवो रामस्तृणबिन्दुर्महामुनिः । पिप्पलादोऽथ वायुश्च संवर्तः पुलहः कचः

47.10.sa: काश्यपश्च पुलस्त्यश्च क्रतुर्दक्षः पराशरः । मरीचिरङ्गिराः काश्यो गौतमो गालवो मुनिः

47.11.sa: धौम्यो विभाण्डो माण्डव्यो धौम्रः कृष्णानुभौतिकः । उलूकः परमो विप्रो मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः

47.12.sa: भास्करिः पूरणः कृष्णः सूतः परमधार्मिकः । एतैश्चान्यैर्मुनिगणैर्महाभागैर्महात्मभिः

47.13.sa: श्रद्धा-दम-शमोपेतैर्वृतश्चन्द्र इव ग्रहैः । भीष्मस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रः कर्मणा मनसा गिरा

47.14.sa: शरतल्पगतः कृष्णं प्रदध्यौ प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः । स्वरेण हृष्टपुष्टेन तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम्
47.14.en: Lying on his bed of arrows, that foremost of men, Bhishma, with pure hearts and joined hands, thought of Krishna in mind, word, and deed. Every sort of excitement is quietly controlled by self-control. One who is not selfcontrolled fails in a similar endeavour. The self-controlled man sees his numberless focs (such as lust, desire, and anger, etc.') as if these dwell in a separate body.

47.15.sa: योगेश्वरं पद्मनाभं विष्णुं जिष्णुं जगत्पतिम् । कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा वाग्विदां प्रवरः प्रभुः । भीष्मः परमधर्मात्मा वासुदेवमथास्तुवत्
47.15.en: With joined hands, that foremost of orators, that powerful Bhishma of highly virtuous soul, thus praised Vasudeva. In all the modes of life, the practice of selfcontrol is distinguished above all other virtues. The fruits of self-control are much greater than those obtainable in all the modes of life.

47.16.sa: आरिराधयिषुः कृष्णं वाचं जिगदिषामियाम् । तया व्याससमासिन्या प्रीयतां पुरुषोत्तमः
47.16.en: Bhishma said "O Krishna, O foremost of Beings, be pleased with words with I utter, in brief and in full, from desire of singing your praises. I shall now describe the characteristic marks of those persons who value self-control highly. They are nobility, calmness of nature, contentment, faith, forgiveness, invariable simplicity, the absence of talk-activeness, humility, reverence for elders, benevolence, mercy for all creatures, frankness, abstention from talk upon kings and men in authority, from all false and useless topics, and from applause and censure of others. The selfcontrolled man becomes desirous of liberation and, quietly bearing present joys and griefs, is never overjoyed or depressed by prospective (Ones.

47.17.sa: शुचिं शुचिपदं हंसं तत्पदं परमेष्ठिनम् । मुक्त्वा सर्वात्मनाऽऽत्मानं तं प्रपद्ये प्रजापतिम्
47.17.en: You are pure and purity. You transcend all. You are what people say to be THAT. You are the Supreme Lord. With my entire heart I seek your refuge, O universal Soul and Lord of all creatures! Shom of vindictiveness and all sorts of guile, and unaffected by praise and censure, such a man is well-behaved, has good manners is pure of soul, had fortitude, and is a complete master of his passions.

47.18.sa: अनाद्यन्तं परं ब्रह्म न देवा नर्षयो विदुः । एकोऽयं वेद भगवान् धाता नारायणो हरिः
47.18.en: You are without beginning and without end. You are the greatest of the great and Brahma. Neither the celestials nor the Rishis know you. The divine Creator, Narayana or Hari, alone knows you. Gaining honours in this world, such a man in after life goes to heaven. Making all creatures gain what they cannot acquire without his help, such a man rejoices and becomes happy.

47.19.sa: नारायणादृषिगणास्तथा सिद्धमहोरगाः । देवा देवर्षयश्चैव यं विदुः परमव्ययम्
47.19.en: Through Narayana, the Rishis, the Siddhas, the great Nagas, the gods, and the celestial Rishis, know a little of you. You are the greatest of the great and undecaying. Devoted to universal benevolence, such a man never feels animosity for any one. Tranquil like a calm ocean, wisdom feels his soul and he is ever cheerful.

47.20.sa: देवदानवगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः । यं न जानन्ति को ह्येष कुतो वा भगवानिति
47.20.en: The celestials, the Danavas, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Pannagas, do not know who you are and whence you have sprung. Endued with intelligence, and deserving of universal reverence, the self-controlled man never fears any creature and is feared by no creature in return.

47.21.sa: यस्मिन्विश्वानि भूतानि तिष्ठन्ति च विशन्ति च । गुणभूतानि भूतेशे सूत्रे मणिगणा इव
47.21.en: All the worlds and all created things live in you and enter you at the time of dissolution. Like gems strung together in a thread, all things possessing attributes exist in you, the Supreme Lord. That man who never rejoices even at large accessions and never feels sorrow when overtaken by misfortune, is said to be endued with contented wisdom. Such a man is said to he self-controlled. Indeed, such a man is said to be a twice-born man.

47.22.sa: यस्मिन्नित्ये तते तन्तौ दृढे स्रगिव तिष्ठति । सदसद्ग्रथितं विश्वं विश्वाङ्गे विश्वकर्मणि
47.22.en: Having the universe for your work and the universe for your limbs, this universe consisting of mind and matter exists in your eternal and all-pervading soul like flowers strung together in a strong thread. Well-read in the scriptures and gifted with a pure soul, the man of self-controi, performing all those acts that are done by the good, enjoys their high fruits.

47.23.en: You are called Hari, have a thousand heads, thousand feet, thousand eyes, thousand arms, thousand crowns, and thousand effulgent faces. You are called Narayana, the deity, and the refuge of the universe. The wicked men, however, never follow the path of benevolence, forgiveness, tranquillity, contentment, sweetness of speech, trutli, liberality, and comfort.

47.24.sa: प्राहुर्नारायणं देवं यं विश्वस्य परायणम् । अणीयसामणीयांसं स्थविष्ठं च स्थवीयसाम्
47.24.en: You are the subtilest of the subtile, grossest of the gross, the heaviest of the heavy, and the highest of the high. They follow the path of lust, anger, cupidity, envy of others, and boastfulness. Overcoming lust and anger, practising the vow of Brahmacharya and becoming a complete master of his senses, the Brahman practising patiently the austerest penances, and observing the most rigid restraints, should live in this world, calmly waiting for his time like one seeming to have a body through fully knowing that he is not subject to destruction.

47.25.sa: गरीयसां गरिष्ठं च श्रेष्ठं च श्रेयसामपि
47.25.en: In the Vaks, the Anuvaks, the Nishads, and the Upanishads, you are regarded as the Supreme Being of irresistible power. In the Samans also, which are always true, you are known as Truth's self.

47.26.sa: यं वाकेष्वनुवाकेषु निषत्सूपनिषत्सु च । गृणन्ति सत्यकर्माणं सत्यं सत्येषु सामसु

47.27.sa: चतुर्भिश्चतुरात्मानं सत्त्वस्थं सात्वतां पतिम् । यं दिव्यैर्देवमर्चन्ति गुह्यैः परमनामभिः
47.27.en: You are of quadruple soul, Supreme soul, individual soul, mind and consciousness. You manifest yourself only in the understanding of all creatures. You are the Lord of your votaries. O god, you are worshipped under four good, high, and secret names, Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha.

47.28.sa: यस्मिन्नित्यं तपस्तप्तं यदङ्गेष्वनुतिष्ठति । सर्वात्मा सर्ववित्सर्वः सर्वज्ञः सर्वभावनः
47.28.en: Penances are always present in you, penances, live in your form. You are the Universal Soul. You are omniscient. You are the universe. You are the creator of everything in the universe.

47.29.sa: यं देवं देवकी देवी वसुदेवादजीजनत् । भौमस्य ब्रह्मणो गुप्त्यै दीप्तमग्निमिवारणिः
47.29.en: Like two sticks creating a blazing fire, you have been born of the divine Devaki and Vasudeva for the protection of Brahma on Earth.

47.30.sa: यमनन्यो व्यपेताशीरात्मानं वीतकल्मषम् । दृष्ट्यानन्त्याय गोविन्दं पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि
47.30.en: For his eternal liberation, the devout worshipper, withdrawing his mind from everything else and renouncing all desires, beholds you, O Govinda, who are the pure Soul, in his own soul.

47.31.en: In the Puranas, you have been described as Purusha. In the beginning of cycles, you are said to be Brahma, and at the time of universal dissolution you are spoken of as Sankarshana. You are worshipful therefore I worship you. are

47.32.sa: पुराणे पुरुषं प्रोक्तं ब्रह्म प्रोक्तं युगादिषु । क्षये सङ्कर्षणं प्रोक्तं तमुपास्यमुपास्महे

47.33.sa: यमेकं बहुधाऽऽत्मानं प्रादुर्भूतमधोक्षजम् । नान्यभक्ताः क्रियावन्तो यजन्ते सर्वकामदम्
47.33.en: Though one, you have yet many forms. You have your passions under complete control. Faithfully performing the rites laid down in the scriptures, your votaries sacrifice to you, O giver of every wish.

47.34.sa: यमाहुर्जगतः कोशं यस्मिन्सन्निहिताः प्रजाः । यस्मिल्लोकाः स्फुरन्तीमे जले शकुनयो यथा
47.34.en: You are designated the sac within which the universe lies. All created things reside in you. Like swans and ducks swimming on the water, all the worlds are seen floating in you.

47.35.sa: ऋतमेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म यत्तत्सदसतोः परम् । अनादिमध्यपर्यन्तं न देवा नर्षयो विदुः । यं सुरासुरगन्धर्वाः सिद्धा ऋषिमहोरगाः
47.35.en: You are Truth. Truth. You One and Undecaying. You are Brahma. You are beyond mind and matter. You are without beginning, middle, and end. Neither the gods nor the Rishis know you.

47.36.sa: प्रयता नित्यमर्चन्ति परमं दुःखभेषजम् । अनादिनिधनं देवमात्मयोनिं सनातनम्
47.36.en: The gods, the Asuras, the Gandharvas, the Siddhas, the Rishis, and the great Uragas, with concentrated minds, always worship you. You are the great panacea for all sorrow.

47.37.sa: अप्रेक्ष्यमनभिज्ञेयं हरिं नारायणं प्रभुम् । यं वै विश्वस्य कर्तारं जगतस्तस्थुषां पतिम् । वदन्ति जगतोऽध्यक्षमक्षरं परमं पदम्
47.37.en: The Vedas describe you as the Creator of the universe and the Lord of everything existing in the universe. You are the Supreme Protector of the universe. You are Undecaying and that which is called the Highest.

47.38.sa: अथ भीष्मस्तवराजः । हिरण्यवर्णं यं गर्भमदितेर्दैत्यनाशनम् । एकं द्वादशधा जज्ञे तस्मै सूर्यात्मने नमः
47.38.en: You are gold-hued. You are the killer of Asuras. Though One, Aditi gave birth to you in twelve forms. Salutations to you who are the Soul of the Sun.

47.39.sa: शुक्ले देवान्पितॄन्कृष्णे तर्पयत्यमृतेन यः । यश्च राजा द्विजातीनां तस्मै सोमात्मने नमः
47.39.en: Salutations to you in your form of Soma who is the highest of Rishis and who gratified with nectar the gods in the light fortnight and the Pitris in the dark fortnight.

47.40.sa: महतस्तमसः पारे पुरुषं ह्यतितेजसम् । यं ज्ञात्वा मृत्युमत्येति तस्मै ज्ञेयात्मने नमः
47.40.en: You are the One Being of transcendent effulgence dwelling beyond darkness Knowing you one has no fear of death. Salutations of you in that form which is an object of knowledge.

47.41.sa: यं बृहन्तं बृहत्युक्थे यमग्नौ यं महाध्वरे । यं विप्रसंघा गायन्ति तस्मै वेदात्मने नमः
47.41.en: In the grand Ukthya sacrifice, the Brahmanas worship you as the great Rich. In the great fire-sacrifice, they describe you as the chief (priest). You are the soul of the Vedas. Salutations to you.

47.42.sa: ऋग्यजुःसामधामानं दशार्धहविरात्मकम् । यं सप्ततन्तुं तन्वन्ति तस्मै यज्ञात्मने नमः
47.42.en: The Rishis, the Yajus, and the Samans are your habitation. You are the five sorts of pure libations. You are the five sorts of pure libations. You are the seven words used in the Vedas. Salutations to you in your form of Sacrifice.

47.43.sa: चतुर्भिश्च चतुर्भिश्च द्वाभ्यां पञ्चभिरेव च । हूयते च पुनर्द्वाभ्यां तस्मै होमात्मने नमः
47.43.en: Libations are poured on the Homa fire accompanied with seventeen Mantras. You are the soul of the Homa. Salutations to you.

47.44.sa: यः सुपर्णो यजुर्नाम च्छन्दोगात्रस्त्रिवृच्छिराः । रथन्तरं वृहत्साम तस्मै स्तोत्रात्मने नमः
47.44.en: You are the Purusha described in the Vedas. Your name is Yajus. The Vedic metres are your limbs. The sacrifices laid down in the three Vedas forın your three heads. The great sacrifices called Rathantara is your voice expressing your gratification. Salutations to you in your form of sacred hymns.

47.45.sa: यः सहस्रसमे सत्रे जज्ञे विश्वसृजामृषिः । हिरण्यपक्षः शकुनिस्तस्मै हंसात्मने नमः
47.45.en: You are the Rishi who had appeared in the great sacrifice extending for a thousand years celebrated by the Patriarchs. You are the great swan with wings of gold. Salutations to you in your form of a swan.

47.46.sa: पादाङ्गं सन्धिपर्वाणं स्वरव्यञ्जनभूषणम् । यमाहुरक्षरं दिव्यं तस्मै वागात्मने नमः
47.46.en: Roots with all kinds of affixes and suffixes form your limbs. The Sandhis are your joints. The consonants and vowels are your ornaments. The Vedas have described you as the divine word. Salutations to you in your form as the Word.

47.47.sa: यज्ञाङ्गो यो वराहो वै भूत्वा गामुज्जहार ह । लोकत्रयहितार्थाय तस्मै वीर्यात्मने नमः
47.47.en: Assuming the form of a boar whose limbs were Sacrifice, you had raised the submerged Earth for the behoof of the three worlds. Salutations to you in your form of infinite power.

47.48.sa: यः शेते योगमास्थाय पर्यङ्के नागभूषिते । फणासहस्ररचिते तस्मै निद्रात्मने नमः
47.48.en: You sleep in Yoga on your snake sofa formed by the thousand hoods (of the Naga). Salutations to you in your forms of sleep.

47.49.sa: यस्तनोति सतां सेतुमृतेनामृतयोनिना । धर्मार्थव्यवहाराङ्गैस्तस्मै सत्यात्मने नमः
47.49.en: You make the bridge for crossing the sea of life with Truth, with the means of emancipation, and with the means by which the senses may be controlled. Salutations to thee in your form of Truth.

47.50.sa: यं पृथग्धर्मचरणाः पृथग्धर्मफलैषिणः । पृथग्धर्मैः समर्चन्ति तस्मै धर्मात्मने नमः
47.50.en: Men following various religions moved by desire of various fruits, worship you with various rites. Salutations to you in your form of religion.

47.51.sa: यतः सर्वं प्रसूयन्ते ह्यनङ्गात्माङ्गदेहिनः । उन्मादः सर्वभूतानां तस्मै कामात्मने नमः
47.51.en: From you have originated all things. You move all creatures having physical frames and cherishing desires to action. Salutations to thee in your form of Excitement.

47.52.sa: यं च व्यक्तस्थमव्यक्तं विचिन्वन्ति महर्षयः । क्षेत्रे क्षेत्रज्ञमासीनं तस्मै क्षेत्रात्मने नमः
47.52.en: The great Rishis seek your unmanifest self within the manifest. Called Kshetrajna, you sit in Kshetra. Salutations to you in your form of Kshetra.

47.53.sa: यं त्रिधात्मानमात्मस्थं वृतं षोडशभिर्गुणैः । प्राहुः सप्तदशं साङ्ख्यास्तस्मै साङ्ख्यात्मने नमः
47.53.en: Though always conscious and present in self, the Sankhyas still describe you as existing in the three states of wakefulness, dream and sleep. They further describe you as possessed of sixteen attributes and representing the number seventeen. Salutations to your form as described by the Sankhyas.

47.54.sa: यं विनिद्रा जितश्वासाः सत्त्वस्थाः संयतेन्द्रियाः । ज्योतिः पश्यन्ति युञ्जानास्तस्मै योगात्मने नमः
47.54.en: Casting off sleep, restraining vital airs, Yogins of controlled senses see you as eternal light. Salutations to you in your Yoga form.

47.55.sa: अपुण्यपुण्योपरमे यं पुनर्भवनिर्भयाः । शान्ताः संन्यासिनो यान्ति तस्मै मोक्षात्मने नमः
47.55.en: Peaceful Sannyasins, freed from fear of rebirth on account of the extinction of all their sins and merits, obtain you. Salutations to you in your form of emancipation.

47.56.sa: योऽसौ युगसहस्रान्ते प्रदीप्तार्चिर्विभावसुः । सम्भक्षयति भूतानि तस्मै घोरात्मने नमः
47.56.en: At the end of a thousand cycles, you assume the form of a fire with blazing flames and consume all creatures. Salutations to you in your form of fierceness.

47.57.sa: सम्भक्ष्य सर्वभूतानि कृत्वा चैकार्णवं जगत् । बालः स्वपिति यश्चैकस्तस्मै मायात्मने नमः
47.57.en: Having consumed all creatures and converted the universe into one sheet of water, you sleep on the waters in the form of a child. Salutations to you in your form as Maya (illusion).

47.58.sa: तद्यस्य नाभ्यां सम्भूतं यस्मिन्विश्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । पुष्करे पुष्कराक्षस्य तस्मै पद्मात्मने नमः
47.58.en: From the navel of the Self-born having eyes like lotus leaves, sprung a lotus. On that lotus is situate this universe. Salutations to you in your form as lotus.

47.59.sa: सहस्रशिरसे चैव पुरुषायामितात्मने । चतुः समुद्रपर्याययोगनिद्रात्मने नमः
47.59.en: You have a thousand heads. You permeate everything. You are of immeasurable soul. You have conquered the four kinds of desire that are as vast as the four seas. Salutations to you in your form of Yoga sleep.

47.60.sa: यस्य केशेषु जीमूता नद्यः सर्वाङ्गसन्धिषु । कुक्षौ समुद्राश्चत्वारस्तस्मै तोयात्मने नमः
47.60.en: The clouds are in the hair of your head. The rivers are in the several joints of your limbs. The four oceans are in your stomach. Salutations to you in your form as water.

47.61.sa: यस्मात्सर्वाः प्रसूयन्ते सर्गप्रलयविक्रियाः । यस्मिंश्चैव प्रलीयन्ते तस्मै हेत्वात्मने नमः
47.61.en: Birth and death originate from you. All things, again, at the universal dissolution, are dissolved in you. Salutations to your form as cause.

47.62.sa: यो निषण्णो भवेद्रात्रौ दिवा भवति विष्ठितः । इष्टानिष्टस्य च द्रष्टा तस्मै द्रष्ट्रात्मने नमः
47.62.en: You sleep not in the night. You are engaged in day time also. You witness the good and the bad actions (of all), Salutations to you in your form of (universal) observer.

47.63.sa: अकुण्ठं सर्वकार्येषु धर्मकार्यार्थमुद्यतम् । वैकुण्ठस्य च तद्रूपं तस्मै कार्यात्मने नमः
47.63.en: There is no act which you cannot do. You are again, always ready to do righteous acts. Salutations to you in your form of Work, the form, viz., which is called Vaikuntha.

47.64.sa: त्रिःसप्तकृत्वो यः क्षत्रं धर्मव्युत्क्रान्तगौरवम् । क्रुद्धो निजघ्ने समरे तस्मै क्रौर्यात्मने नमः
47.64.en: In anger you had in battle, rooted out twenty-one times the Kshatriyas who had trodden virtue and authority under their feet, Salutations to you in your form of Cruelty.

47.65.sa: विभज्य पञ्चधाऽऽत्मानं वायुर्भूत्वा शरीरगः । यश्चेष्टयति भूतानि तस्मै वाय्वात्मने नमः
47.65.en: Dividing yourself into five parts you have become the five vital airs which work within every body and cause every living creature to inove. Salutations to you in your form of air.

47.66.sa: युगेष्वावर्तते योगैर्मासर्त्वयनहायनैः । सर्गप्रलययोः कर्ता तस्मै कालात्मने नमः
47.66.en: You appear in very cycle in the forms called month and season and half-year and year, and are the cause of both creation and dissolution. Salutations to you in your form of Time.

47.67.sa: ब्रह्म वक्त्रं भुजौ क्षत्रं कृत्स्नमूरूदरं विशः । पादौ यस्याश्रिताः शूद्रास्तस्मै वर्णात्मने नमः
47.67.en: Brahmanas are your mouth, Kshatriyas are your two arms., Vaishyas are your stomach and thighs, and Shudras are your feet. Salutations to you in your form of caste.

47.68.sa: यस्याग्निरास्यं द्यौर्मूर्धा खं नाभिश्चरणौ क्षितिः । सूर्यश्चक्षुर्दिशः श्रोत्रे तस्मै लोकात्मने नमः
47.68.en: Fire is your mouth. The heavens are the crown of your head. The sky in your navel. The Earth is your feet. The Sun is your eye. The points of horizon are your ears. Salutations to you in your form as the three worlds.

47.69.sa: परः कालात्परो यज्ञात्परात्परतरश्च यः । अनादिरादिर्विश्वस्य तस्मै विश्वात्मने नमः
47.69.en: You are superior to Time. You are superior to Sacrifice. You are higher than the highest. Having yourself no origin, you are the origin of the Universe. Salutations to you in your form as Universe.

47.70.sa: विषये वर्तमानानां यं तं वैशेषिकैर्गुणैः । प्राहुर्विषयगोप्तारं तस्मै गोप्त्रात्मने नमः
47.70.en: People according to the attributes assigned to you by the Vaisheshika theory, consider you as the Protector of the world. Salutations to you in your form of Protector.

47.71.sa: अन्नपानेन्धनमयो रसप्राणविवर्धनः । यो धारयति भूतानि तस्मै प्राणात्मने नमः
47.71.en: Assuming the forms of food, drink, and fuel, you multiply the humours and the vital airs of creatures and keep up their existence. Salutations to you in your form of life.

47.72.sa: प्राणानां धारणार्थाय योऽन्नं भुङ्क्ते चतुर्विधम् । अन्तर्भूतः पचत्यग्निस्तस्मै पाकात्मने नमः
47.72.en: For supporting the life you eat the four kinds of food. Assuming also the form of Agni within the Stomach, you digest that food. Salutations to you in you form of digesting fire.

47.73.sa: पिङ्गेक्षणसटं यस्य रूपं दंष्ट्रानखायुधम् । दानवेन्द्रान्तकरणं तस्मै दृप्तात्मने नमः
47.73.en: Assuming the form of man-lion with twany eyes and twany manes with teeth and claws for your weapons, you had killed the king of the Asuras. Salutations to your form of great subtility.

47.74.sa: यं न देवा न गन्धर्वा न दैत्या न च दानवाः । तत्त्वतो हि विजानन्ति तस्मै सूक्ष्मात्मने नमः
47.74.en: The gods, the Gandharvas, Daityas and Danavas are not able understand that form corectly, I salute that form of subtile.

47.75.sa: रसातलगतः श्रीमाननन्तो भगवान्विभुः । जगद्धारयते कृत्स्नं तस्मै वीर्यात्मने नमः
47.75.en: Assuming the form of the beautiful, illustrious, and powerful Ananta in the neither region, you uphold the universe. Salutations to your form of power.

47.76.sa: यो मोहयति भूतानि स्नेहपाशानुबन्धनैः । सर्गस्य रक्षणार्थाय तस्मै मोहात्मने नमः
47.76.en: You stupefy all creatures by the letters of affection and love for the continuance of the creation. Salutations to you in your form of stupefaction.

47.77.sa: आत्मज्ञानमिदं ज्ञानं ज्ञात्वा पञ्चस्ववस्थितम् । यं ज्ञानेनाभिगच्छन्ति तस्मै ज्ञानात्मने नमः
47.77.en: Knowing that knowledge which knows the five elements to be the true Self-knowledge people approach you by knowledge. Salutations to you in your form of Knowledge.

47.78.sa: अप्रमेयशरीराय सर्वतो बुद्धिचक्षुषे । अनन्तपरिमेयाय तस्मै दिव्यात्मने नमः
47.78.en: Your body cannot be measured. Your understanding and eyes see every thing. You are infinite and immeasurable. Salutations to you in your form of vastness.

47.79.sa: जटिने दण्डिने नित्यं लम्बोदरशरीरिणे । कमण्डलुनिषङ्गाय तस्मै ब्रह्मात्मने नमः
47.79.en: You had assumed the form of a hermit with matted locks on head, staff in hand, a long stomach, and having alms bowl for your quiver. Salutations to your form of Brahma.

47.80.sa: शूलिने त्रिदशेशाय त्र्यम्बकाय महात्मने । भस्मदिग्धोर्ध्वलिङ्गाय तस्मै रुद्रात्मने नमः
47.80.en: You carry the trident, you are the lord of the celestials, you have three eyes, and you are great. Your body is always besmeared with ashes. Salutations to you in your form of Rudra.

47.81.sa: चन्द्राधकृतशीर्षाय व्यालयज्ञोपवीतिने । पिनाकशूलहस्ताय तस्मै उग्रात्मने नमः
47.81.en: The crescent forms the ornament of your forehead. You have snakes for the holy thread round your neck. You are armed with Pinaka and trident. Salutations to your form of dreadfulness.

47.82.sa: सर्वभूतात्मभूताय भूतादिनिधनाय च । अक्रोधद्रोहमोहाय तस्मै शान्तात्मने नमः
47.82.en: You are the soul of all creatures. You are the Creator and the Destroyer of all creatures. You are without anger, without enmity, without affection. Salutations to you in your form of Peace.

47.83.sa: यस्मिन्सर्वं यतः सर्वं यः सर्वं सर्वतश्च यः । यश्च सर्वमयो नित्यं तस्मै सर्वात्मने नमः
47.83.en: Everything is in you. Everything originates from you. You are Everything. Everywhere are you. You are always the All. Salutations to you in your form as Everything.

47.84.sa: विश्वकर्मन्नमस्तेऽस्तु विश्वात्मन्विश्वसम्भव । अपवर्गस्थभूतानां पञ्चानां परतः स्थितः
47.84.en: Salutations to you whose work is the universe, to you who are the soul of the universe, to you from whom has originated the universe, to you who are the dissolution of all things, to you who are beyond the five elements.

47.85.sa: नमस्ते त्रिषु लोकेषु नमस्ते परतस्त्रिषु । नमस्ते दिक्षु सर्वासु त्वं हि सर्वमयो निधिः
47.85.en: Salutations to you who are the three worlds to you who are above the three worlds! Salutations to you who are all the directions. You are all you are the one refuge of All.

47.86.sa: नमस्ते भगवन्विष्णो लोकानां प्रभवाप्यय । त्वं हि कर्ता हृषीकेश संहर्ता चापराजितः
47.86.en: Salutations to you. O divine Lord, O Vishnu, and, O eternal origin of all the worlds. You, O Hrishikesha, are the Creator, you are the Destroyer, and you are invincible.

47.87.sa: न हि पश्यामि ते भावं दिव्यं हि त्रिषु वर्त्मसु । त्वां तु पश्यामि तत्त्वेन यत्ते रूपं सनातनम्
47.87.en: I cannot see that divine form in which you are manifest in the Past, Present, and Future. I can, however, see truly your eternal form.

47.88.sa: दिवं ते शिरसा व्याप्तं पद्भ्यां देवी वसुन्धरा । विक्रमेण त्रयो लोकाः पुरुषोऽसि सनातनः
47.88.en: You have filled heaven with your head, and Earth with your, and feet the three worlds with your energy. You are Eternal. and permeate everything in the universe.

47.89.sa: दिशो भुजा रविश्चक्षुर्वीर्ये शुक्रः प्रतिष्ठितः । सप्तमार्गा निरुद्धास्ते वायोरमिततेजसः
47.89.en: The directions are your arms, the Sun is your eye, and prowess is your arms, the Sun is your eye, and prowess is your vital fluid. You are the lord of all creatures. You stand closing the seven paths of the Wind whose power is immeasurable.

47.90.sa: अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीतवाससमच्युतम् । ये नमस्यन्ति गोविन्दं न तेषां विद्यते भयम्
47.90.en: Those who worship you, are freed from all fears, O Govinda of undecaying prowess, you are clad in yellow robes of the colour of the Atasi flower.

47.91.sa: एकोऽपि कृष्णस्य कृतः प्रणामो दशाश्वमेधावभृथेन तुल्यः । दशाश्वमेधी पुनरेति जन्म कृष्णप्रणामी न पुनर्भवाय
47.91.en: The lowering of head to you for once. O Krishna, is equal to the completion of ten Horse-sacrifices. The man who has celebrated ten Horse-sacrifices is not freed from the obligation of re-birth.

47.92.sa: कृष्णव्रताः कृष्णमनुस्मरन्तो रात्रौ च कृष्णं पुनरुत्थिता ये । ते कृष्णदेहाः प्रविशन्ति कृष्णमाज्यं यथा मन्त्रहुतं हुताशे
47.92.en: The man, however, that salutes Krishna is freed from re-birth. They who have Krishna for their vow, they who think of Krishna in the night, and upon getting up from sleep, may be said to have Krishna for their body.
